title: Credit Builder Accounts Early-Closure Returned-Fee Relief by Kind of Returned Payment
content:
The early-closure returned-fee relief on a Credit Builder account depends on what kind of payment the most recent returned payment was. The rule acts on the amount the relief share gives on the returned-payment fee, and the relief is rounded to the cent after it.

## Rule

- When that returned payment was an AutoPay debit (the payment its return line points at was made through the AutoPay channel), the relief is reduced by one sixtieth for each calendar day after the return date up to and including the date of the pending early-closure request, a request registered before the return date counting no days, and never below zero.
- When it was any other payment for less than the monthly payment, the relief is halved.
- When it was any other payment for the monthly payment or more, the relief keeps its full amount.

The return line is the returned-payment entry; it names the payment it reverses, and that payment entry shows the channel it was made through. The return date is the date of the return line; the request date is the day the pending early-closure request was registered. In the AutoPay case the relief is multiplied by 1 less the number of days divided by 60, and is zero from 60 days on.

| Returned payment | Request registered | Relief |
|---|---|---|
| AutoPay debit | on the return date | full (0 days) |
| AutoPay debit | 12 days after the return date | 48 sixtieths |
| AutoPay debit | 60 or more days after | zero |
| AutoPay debit | before the return date | full (no days counted) |
| other payment, below the monthly payment | any | halved |
| other payment, the monthly payment or more | any | full |

## Hypothetical figures

The relief share gives 3.00 on the fee. An AutoPay debit returned on 2 May with the request registered on 14 May: 12 days, 3.00 times 48 divided by 60, that is 2.40. A one-time payment of 40.00 on a plan with a monthly payment of 100.00: 1.50.
